text.p: The main yard of bankrupt shipbuilding group Bremer Vulkan on Wednesday gained a reprieve as the state of Bremen granted a 42 million-mark ($27.24 million) loan guarantee, preventing its immediate closure.
But the city government said the yard would have to cease its merchant shipbuilding activities, which employ about 1,000 workers, by mid-1997.
Bremer Vulkan's administrator Jobst Wellensiek said the loan guarantee would allow the completion of a container ship, thereby keeping the yard in business at least until April 1997.

The Bremen government said it would be prepared to provide a second loan guarantee to allow the yard to complete a second ship, provided that Wellensiek could arrange the funding. In that case the yard could stay open until mid-1997.

The Bremer Vulkan group collapsed in May after posting huge losses and being accused of having misappropriated hundreds of millions of marks in state aid cleared by the European Union for use in eastern Germany.
The shipyards were one of the region's largest employers and their collapse has sent the unemployment rate, already above the national average, sharply higher.
